semantic_rule: A nonzero divider color (the modal nonzero color) fills the rows and columns at offsets 4, 9, 14, ... over a 0 background, forming a lattice of cells that each hold at most one small same-color block. The output is a staircase: one row per non-divider, nonzero color whose length equals that color's 4-connected block count, rows sorted by count ascending and 0-padded to the maximum count. Divider-colored blocks are distractors excluded from the count.
shortcut_hypotheses_checked: count-cells-instead-of-objects: medium/hard draws include non-2x2 single-component polyominoes (90-100% of draws), so cell counting predicts a different staircase width than the oracle
sort-by-color or reading order instead of sort-by-count: counted colors are shuffled from the palette and counts are pairwise distinct, so color order and count order decorrelate
count divider-colored blocks too: divider-colored distractor blocks appear in 25-58% of draws per band and the oracle excludes them (mode-color exclusion branch witnessed)
modal-color echo: output palette never contains the input's modal colors (0 and the divider color); modal cells only ever play the background/divider role
marker-as-answer: no marker cells; block positions are shuffled per draw and carry no output information beyond component counts
dimension-only prediction: output dims (color_count x max count) vary independently of input dims (11..29 lattice sizes); 5 distinct output shapes across 300 probed pairs
constant/no-op output: rule_smoke fired 120/120 with 119 distinct outputs; identity rate 0%

semantic_rule: A nonzero divider color (the modal nonzero color) fills the rows and columns at offsets 4, 9, 14, ... over a 0 background, forming a lattice of cells that each hold at most one small same-color block. The output is a staircase: one row per non-divider, nonzero color whose length equals that color's 4-connected block count, rows sorted by count ascending and 0-padded to the maximum count. Divider-colored blocks are distractors excluded from the count.
shortcut_hypotheses_checked: count-cells-instead-of-objects: medium/hard draws include non-2x2 single-component polyominoes (90-100% of draws), so cell counting predicts a different staircase width than the oracle
sort-by-color or reading order instead of sort-by-count: counted colors are shuffled from the palette and counts are pairwise distinct, so color order and count order decorrelate
count divider-colored blocks too: divider-colored distractor blocks appear in 25-58% of draws per band and the oracle excludes them (mode-color exclusion branch witnessed)
modal-color echo: output palette never contains the input's modal colors (0 and the divider color); modal cells only ever play the background/divider role
marker-as-answer: no marker cells; block positions are shuffled per draw and carry no output information beyond component counts
dimension-only prediction: output dims (color_count x max count) vary independently of input dims (11..29 lattice sizes); 5 distinct output shapes across 300 probed pairs

semantic_rule: On an azure (8) background with exactly one full-width red (2) row (the line), every 4-connected color-1 shape above the line falls downward. A thin shape (every row holds a single cell, i.e. a vertical bar or singleton) falls through the line until its lowest cell lands on the grid's last row and punches an 8-hole in the line at each of its columns. A wide shape (some row holds >=2 cells) falls until its lowest wide row rests on the row just above the line; any thin tail below that wide row overwrites line cells and can extend below the line. Original shape cells above the line are erased to the 8 background.

semantic_rule: A nonzero divider color (the modal nonzero color) fills the rows and columns at offsets 4, 9, 14, ... over a 0 background, forming a lattice of cells that each hold at most one small same-color block. The output is a staircase: one row per non-divider, nonzero color whose length equals that color's 4-connected block count, rows sorted by count ascending and 0-padded to the maximum count. Divider-colored blocks are distractors excluded from the count.

semantic_rule: On an azure (8) background with exactly one full-width red (2) row (the line), every 4-connected color-1 shape above the line falls downward. A thin shape (every row holds a single cell, i.e. a vertical bar or singleton) falls through the line until its lowest cell lands on the grid's last row and punches an 8-hole in the line at each of its columns. A wide shape (some row holds >=2 cells) falls until its lowest wide row rests on the row just above the line; any thin tail below that wide row overwrites line cells and can extend below the line. Original shape cells above the line are erased to the 8 background.

semantic_rule: A tall narrow grid has one all-2 separator row, one contiguous bar row above and one below in a shared non-{2,4} color. Columns present in BOTH bars are filled with 4 between the strictly wider bar and the separator; the narrower side never fills.

fill both gaps around the separator -> every demo fills only the wider side
fill always above / always below -> top_wider balanced 31:29, 31:29, 31:29 across easy/medium/hard (180 draws)
use the bar color for the fill -> fill is always 4, bar color varies over 8 non-{2,4} colors
dimension-only prediction -> output dims equal input dims; content varies independently (42/42 parity)
count-only prediction -> fill side needs the width comparison AND the intersection geometry; widths alone do not determine filled columns under non-subset draws
marker-as-answer -> the separator is structural (always h//2), not an answer encoding; fill columns/rows derive from bar geometry
modal-color echo -> fill color 4 is fixed by the rule, unrelated to the input's modal non-zero color
constant-output / identity -> wider bar always keeps >=1 empty row toward the separator and the intersection is non-empty, so every default draw fills (frac_identity=0% at lint)

semantic_rule: Input: 0-background grid with exactly one blue(1) cell on the bottom row. A ball launched from that cell travels upward on a diagonal - initially up-right when the cell sits in column 0, otherwise up-left - reversing horizontal direction at each left/right wall until it exits the top edge. Output: every path cell becomes 1, every other cell becomes 8.
shortcut_hypotheses_checked: dimension-only prediction: with canonical-style fixed corner starts the whole output is determined by (h,w); generator varies the start column across the full width (incl. right-edge and interior), so equal-dims instances yield different outputs
constant-output / modal-color echo: output modal color is always 8 but the blue zigzag path must be computed; h>=4 guarantees a non-trivial path on every draw
marker-as-answer: the blue cell only seeds the path; its column varies lawfully and the bounce direction (up-right only from column 0, else up-left) is a rule property, not a marker lookup
count-only prediction: exactly one object on every draw, so counts carry no answer signal; geometry decides the output

semantic_rule: Row 0 is an ordering legend: its non-zero cells read left-to-right list distinct colors. Rows 2..h-1 (row 1 is an empty separator) hold small 4-connected polyomino pieces. For each legend color, take the LAST piece of that color (latest in reading order: bottom-most, then right-most), crop it to its bounding box keeping internal zeros, and pack the crops horizontally in legend order with 1-column zero gaps, top-aligned, painting only non-zero cells. Output dims: max(piece bbox heights) x (sum of bbox widths + n-1). Duplicate-color pieces make 'last' beat 'first'; pieces of non-legend colors are ignored.

semantic_rule: The bounding box of the yellow(4) cells IS the template (always 3x3 in the demos: yellow body cells plus magenta(6) marker cells, no holes; yellow appears nowhere else). For each of the 8 dihedral orientations of the template, slide it over the grid (bottom/right one-cell overhang allowed). A position matches when every in-bounds template-6 cell sits on a grid-6 cell, no in-bounds template-4 cell sits on a grid-6 cell, and at least 2 template-6 cells hit a grid-6. On a match, every in-bounds template-4 cell is painted 4. The demos are dense fields of noise colors 0/1/8 with ~10-13% magenta, so matches emerge from the noise.

semantic_rule: Vertical pingpong extension: output height = 4*(h-1)+1 (two full zigzag periods of 2*(h-1)), output width = input width. Output row i copies input row pos when pos = i mod 2*(h-1) is <= h-1, else input row 2*(h-1)-pos (reflection). Pure geometric rule on dotted-lattice inputs: sparse 1-2 color short-period marks on a 0 background.

semantic_rule: On an orange(7) background there are exactly two other colors: the MARKER color (least cells -- always a single 5-cell plus shape) and the BLOCK color (most cells -- solid squares of side 1..7). For each 4-connected block object, test whether its bbox has both dimensions odd (odd-sided square). semantic_rule: A gray(5) blob is made of 2x2 'rooms' joined by 1-wide arms. Tip arms: a degree-1 cell grows a straight 3-cell run toward its only neighbor. Bridge arms: an uncovered thin cell (in no 2x2) grows a 3-cell run toward a thick (in-2x2) neighbor, tie-break up/left/down/right. Arm cells recolor to red(2) — including room cells the run overlaps; all other gray cells recolor to cyan(8).

semantic_rule: The grid is an orange(7) chamber inside a magenta(6) perimeter frame. Every interior object is a single-colored cross: a 5-cell plus whose one extended arm is strictly longest (canonical arms [1,1,1,2]). For each cross, find its center (the unique 4-neighbor cell) and its strictly-longest arm; CLEAR the border cell the longest arm faces to 0, and PAINT the opposite border cell with the cross's color. Crosses compose collision-free: horizontal-arm crosses sit in distinct rows and vertical-arm crosses in distinct columns, so no two crosses project onto the same border cell.

semantic_rule: The background is the grid's most frequent NON-ZERO color (the oracle's mode excludes 0 by default). Every 4-connected non-background component consists of EXACTLY TWO colors stacked vertically (each color class itself 4-connected, the upper class's rows strictly above the lower's). For each component independently, the color with the smaller min-row (top) shifts LEFT by 1 and the other (bottom) shifts RIGHT by 1; the output is a fresh background canvas holding only the shifted cells.

semantic_rule: Every 4-connected zero component that touches the top or bottom edge is mirrored vertically to the opposite side; every hole touching the left or right edge is mirrored horizontally. Floating holes are skipped by the mirror but may be consumed by other sweeps.

semantic_rule: Per row, independently: take the non-7 cells' columns in order. If the row contains a color-6 anchor, paint a color-8 bar whose length equals the row's non-7 count, starting at c6 - idx where idx is the 6's column-rank among the non-7 cells. Rows without a 6 become all 7; every other cell becomes 7.

semantic_rule: Every 4-connected zero component that touches the top or bottom edge is mirrored vertically to the opposite side; every hole touching the left or right edge is mirrored horizontally. Floating holes are skipped by the mirror but may be consumed by other sweeps.

semantic_rule: On an orange(7) background there are exactly two other colors: the MARKER color (least cells -- always a single 5-cell plus shape) and the BLOCK color (most cells -- solid squares of side 1..7). For each 4-connected block object, test whether its bbox has both dimensions odd (odd-sided square). If odd-sided blocks outnumber even-sided ones, the plus is KEPT; otherwise it is erased to the background. Either way, every odd-sided block's center cell is painted with the marker color.

semantic_rule: The bounding box of the yellow(4) cells IS the template (always 3x3 in the demos: yellow body cells plus magenta(6) marker cells, no holes; yellow appears nowhere else). For each of the 8 dihedral orientations of the template, slide it over the grid (bottom/right one-cell overhang allowed). A position matches when every in-bounds template-6 cell sits on a grid-6 cell, no in-bounds template-4 cell sits on a grid-6 cell, and at least 2 template-6 cells hit a grid-6. On a match, every in-bounds template-4 cell is painted 4. The demos are dense fields of noise colors 0/1/8 with ~10-13% magenta, so matches emerge from the noise.

Floating holes are skipped by the mirror but may be consumed by other sweeps.

semantic_rule: On an azure (8) background with exactly one full-width red (2) row (the line), every 4-connected color-1 shape above the line falls downward. A thin shape (every row holds a single cell, i.e. a vertical bar or singleton) falls through the line until its lowest cell lands on the grid's last row and punches an 8-hole in the line at each of its columns. A wide shape (some row holds >=2 cells) falls until its lowest wide row rests on the row just above the line; any thin tail below that wide row overwrites line cells and can extend below the line. Original shape cells above the line are erased to the 8 background.

semantic_rule: Row 0 is an ordering legend: its non-zero cells read left-to-right list distinct colors. Rows 2..h-1 (row 1 is an empty separator) hold small 4-connected polyomino pieces. For each legend color, take the LAST piece of that color (latest in reading order: bottom-most, then right-most), crop it to its bounding box keeping internal zeros, and pack the crops horizontally in legend order with 1-column zero gaps, top-aligned, painting only non-zero cells. Output dims: max(piece bbox heights) x (sum of bbox widths + n-1). Duplicate-color pieces make 'last' beat 'first'; pieces of non-legend colors are ignored.

semantic_rule: On an azure (8) background with exactly one full-width red (2) row (the line), every 4-connected color-1 shape above the line falls downward. A thin shape (every row holds a single cell, i.e. a vertical bar or singleton) falls through the line until its lowest cell lands on the grid's last row and punches an 8-hole in the line at each of its columns. A wide shape (some row holds >=2 cells) falls until its lowest wide row rests on the row just above the line; any thin tail below that wide row overwrites line cells and can extend below the line. Original shape cells above the line are erased to the 8 background.

semantic_rule: The grid is an orange(7) chamber inside a magenta(6) perimeter frame. Every interior object is a single-colored cross: a 5-cell plus whose one extended arm is strictly longest (canonical arms [1,1,1,2]). For each cross, find its center (the unique 4-neighbor cell) and its strictly-longest arm; CLEAR the border cell the longest arm faces to 0, and PAINT the opposite border cell with the cross's color. Crosses compose collision-free: horizontal-arm crosses sit in distinct rows and vertical-arm crosses in distinct columns, so no two crosses project onto the same border cell.

Arm cells recolor to red(2) — including room cells the run overlaps; all other gray cells recolor to cyan(8).

semantic_rule: On an azure (8) background with exactly one full-width red (2) row (the line), every 4-connected color-1 shape above the line falls downward. A thin shape (every row holds a single cell, i.e. a vertical bar or singleton) falls through the line until its lowest cell lands on the grid's last row and punches an 8-hole in the line at each of its columns. A wide shape (some row holds >=2 cells) falls until its lowest wide row rests on the row just above the line; any thin tail below that wide row overwrites line cells and can extend below the line. Original shape cells above the line are erased to the 8 background.

semantic_rule: Find the first red 2 source. Infer its inward direction from the source edge in top, bottom, left, right precedence, with rightward fallback for a non-edge source. Advance one cell at a time for at most 500 steps. Stop before a gray 5 or after leaving the grid; otherwise paint the visited cell cyan 8, turn on slash 7 by (dr,dc)=(-dc,-dr), and turn on backslash 6 by (dr,dc)=(dc,dr). The output is an otherwise-zero grid of the same dimensions.

semantic_rule: Let n be the input row count. Build an n-squared by n-squared output whose cell at row r and column c equals the input cell at row r modulo n and column c modulo n. Equivalently, repeat the complete n-by-n input tile n times horizontally and n times vertically, preserving every color and within-tile position.

Repeat only each column vertically: refuted because every source row also repeats across by column residue.
Scale each source cell into an n-by-n solid block: refuted by the alternating within-row pattern of every public output.
All one-color source tiles are equivalent: refuted by seven distinct complete occupancy profiles and exact within-tile positional preservation.
Multicolor is automatically canonical because the oracle supports it: rejected; every public source has exactly one foreground color, so multicolor remains measured minority extrapolation.

semantic_rule: Preserve every nonzero input cell. For each zero cell, scan its column from row zero up to, but not including, the cell's row. If that prefix contains a nonzero value, replace the zero with the first such value; otherwise leave it zero. Thus the topmost seed in each active column drips downward while later nonzero seeds, if present in a broad oracle input, remain unchanged.

semantic_rule: Use the most frequent nonzero color as background. Sort every remaining color by cell count; the largest repeated count becomes a solid upper-right square, the next repeated count becomes a solid lower-left square, and the first singleton color—when one exists—is placed at the bottom-left corner. Square side lengths are the integer roots of their counts. A singleton introduces the demonstrated two-column left offset; without one, the small square starts at column zero.

semantic_rule: Take the first-seen modal color as background and remove non-background corner markers. Merge same-color 8-connected pieces whose union fits a 5x5 motif. In every multi-color motif, treat the most frequent color as body and the least frequent color as core, then swap body and core. An off-center motif can inherit the body color of a congruent centered same-core twin. Finally, stamp every motif at the corner whose marker matches its core; if the motif encloses a hole, stamp only the loop bounding that hole.

Union all auras, preserve all existing red cells, clip naturally at canvas edges, and keep the output dimensions unchanged.

Assume independent non-overlapping auras: overlapping_auras requires union behavior.
Overwrite red reached by another aura: aura_hits_other_bar proves painting is restricted to currently zero cells.
Approximate bbox length with component size: orientation/parity/interaction profiles and exact oracle facts enforce the inclusive maximum bbox dimension.

semantic_rule: Choose the unique modal background and initialize the result as an input copy. First, for each color 1 through 9 except the background, compute its original-input bbox; if that bbox contains at least one other foreground color and no background, fill the entire bbox in the result with the color, with higher colors overwriting lower ones. Second, again in ascending color order, if every original cell of a color lies on one row, column, down diagonal, or up diagonal, traverse between its row-major endpoints and repaint only positions whose original input value is not background. This line pass overwrites rectangle fills and lower line colors; original background gaps remain unchanged.

Fill every color bbox: disconnected_bbox_blocks_fill preserves bboxes containing background.
Use the evolving result for eligibility: line_over_restoration and competing bboxes require facts from the original input.
Support only rows and down diagonals: vertical_bridge and diag_up_bridge cover the missing directions.
Fill background gaps between line endpoints: background_gap_stays preserves those exact cells.
Ignore extra same-color cells: off_line_decoy_disables proves every cell must remain collinear.
Treat disconnected same-color pieces separately: the rule uses all cells of that color in one bbox.
Resolve overlaps by geometry or discovery order: rect_priority requires ascending numeric color order.
Apply lines before rectangle fills: line_over_restoration proves the line pass is last.
Merge simultaneous lines without precedence: multiple_lines_priority requires the higher processed line color at their crossing.

semantic_rule: Take the bounding box of all nonzero input cells. Let its top-left be (r0,c0), its dimensions be bh by bw, its source color be the top-left cell, its complement be 9 minus that color, and its period be bh+bw. At anchors (r0+k*period,c0+sign*k*period), for integer k and both diagonal signs, first stamp every intersecting bw-by-bh quarter-turned rectangle at (anchor_row+bh, anchor_col+(bw if sign is positive else -bh)) in the complementary color, clipping outside the canvas. Then stamp every distinct intersecting bh-by-bw diagonal rectangle in the source color, so source stamps win overlaps.
shortcut_hypotheses_checked: The source is not always 2x3 or 3x2: official 1x3, 4x2, 5x2, and 2x1 anchors plus square and oblong profiles refute fixed-size shortcuts.
The source color is not restricted to canonical 3 and 6: generated evidence exercises every color one through eight and checks exact 9-minus complement.
Rotated stamps do not retain source color: every profile compares against a separate oracle that uses the complementary color.
The period is height plus width, not area or a fixed stride: bars, squares, and varied oblongs force distinct period relationships.
Partially visible stamps are not discarded: corner and edge profiles prove clipped drawing at canvas boundaries.
Overlap order is semantic: source-color diagonal rectangles are stamped last and win every shared cell.
Both diagonal directions and negative period indices matter: generalized placements exercise all canvas quadrants.

Endpoints must have identical dimensions: false; unequal_overlap bridges midpoint-aligned boxes with different heights.

Choose the first window in reading order: false; red-cell count has priority before position.
Break equal red counts by numeric color or arbitrary enumeration: false; top-left row and then column decide the tie.
Recolor all gray cells near red: false; only gray cells in greedily selected 3x3 windows change.
Recolor red cells as part of completing the box: false; every red 2 is preserved.
Use one output color for the whole window: false; the gray center becomes yellow 4 while other selected gray cells become orange 7.

semantic_audit.canonical_like_definition: Returned input exactly matches one official joint geometry signature: 10x10 shape, ordered rectangle (height,width) sequence, ordered left-edge columns, and universal bottom alignment; colors may be any distinct nonzero labels.

stability_census.strict_definition: Returned input exactly matches one official joint geometry signature: 10x10 shape, ordered rectangle (height,width) sequence, ordered left-edge columns, and universal bottom alignment; colors may be any distinct nonzero labels.

semantic_rule: Find every nonzero monochrome solid rectangular component, sort the rectangles by bounding-box left column, and repaint their bounding boxes on a fresh same-size zero grid. The first rectangle starts at (0,0); each next top-left advances by the previous rectangle’s (height−1,width−1), so consecutive rectangles share exactly one corner and the later color owns that corner.
shortcut_hypotheses_checked: Fixed-position/fixed-size shortcut: all official inputs are 10×10, bottom-aligned, compact layouts. Falsified as the sole interpretation by generating lawful mixed/scattered rows, irregular/spread gaps, and varied canvases while preserving exact oracle parity.

Count-only or color-sequence shortcut: varying 2..6 objects and randomly permuting distinct colors is insufficient unless dimensions and left-edge order determine the output. The generated and recombination probes require the ordered bbox dimensions to be preserved in the staircase.

Non-overlapping diagonal packing: the original prose suggested cumulative heights and an arbitrary column spacing. Canonical outputs and Racket probes instead require (height−1,width−1) advances and later-color overwrite at each shared corner.

Sorting by row or color rather than left edge: generalized inputs vary row layout and colors independently while retaining strict left-to-right bbox order; the oracle continues to place rectangles in left-edge order.

sibling_rows.summary: Nested concentric frame blocks; the rule reads layer colors down the bbox diagonal, dedups, reverses, and remaps the whole component. Blocks are square OR rectangular, even OR odd sized (single-cell center), with optionally REPEATED layer colors (dedup makes the swap asymmetric). (Was: square even-size blocks with all-distinct layers only.)

15×17 grid with 3-4 rectangular OUTLINES, each in a distinct non-zero color. Outlines are nested (largest outermost) so the interruption-topology sort is well-defined: each outline's bbox contains the next-smaller outline's bbox. Outline = rectangle border only (interior is 0 / inner outlines). Rule: detect each color's outline rectangle. Compute interruption topology — outline A interrupts B if A's outline crosses any of B's edge cells. Topologically sort colors so interrupters come first (outermost). Output: (2n-1) × (2n-1) square where n = number of colors. Build concentric layers using distance-to-edge: layer k (0=outermost) gets the k-th color in the sort. Output cell at (r, c) = colors[min(r, c, size-1-r, size-1-c)].

0-bg grid (size varies) with a stack of concentric color-4 rectangular frames and k color-2 markers in row 0. Rule: rank frames by area, select the k-th, and fill its interior with 8 down to the next-inner frame. The grid size, frame count, band widths and k vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~27 distinct).

0-bg grid with N (2-4) connected non-bg components, each in its own distinct color, with OVERLAPPING bounding boxes (typically nested rectangle frames). Rule: extract every 4-conn component (objects g 0); for each output cell (r, c), set output[r][c] = the count of objects whose bbox (r1,c1,r2,c2) contains (r,c) (i.e., r1≤r≤r2 AND c1≤c≤c2). Output is a count map; the original colors are DROPPED — values are integers 0..N.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 11-14) with: N_FRAMES ∈ 2-4 NESTED CONCENTRIC COLOR-8 (CYAN) RECTANGULAR FRAMES, drawn from outer-most to inner-most: OUTERMOST at (1, 1)..(h-2, w-2), each subsequent frame 2 cells in on every side (r1 += 2, c1 += 2, r2 -= 2, c2 -= 2). Each frame is a hollow rectangular outline in COLOR 8. All frames have STRICTLY DISTINCT bbox areas by construction (each inner is smaller by 4 rows × 4 cols). Rule (SORT THE 8-FRAMES BY BBOX AREA DESCENDING; ASSIGN EACH FRAME (BY DEPTH RANK 0 = OUTERMOST, 1, 2, ...) A COLOR FROM THE PALETTE [2,4,6,7,3,5,9]; RECOLOR EVERY CELL OF THAT FRAME TO THE ASSIGNED COLOR): EXTRACT every color-8 frame. SORT by BBOX AREA DESCENDING (largest first). For RANK i in 0..n-1: RECOLOR the i-th frame's cells to PALETTE[i] (palette = [2, 4, 6, 7, 3, 5, 9]). Net: cyan frames become rainbow-colored by nesting depth.

0-bg grid (h ∈ 12-20, w ∈ 14-24, by difficulty) with: N_GROUPS ∈ 1-3 FRAME GROUPS laid out horizontally (each group occupies a w//n_groups slot). FOR EACH GROUP: (a) ONE OUTER FRAME — drawn via draw_frame as a rectangular outline of size ofh × ofw (ofh ∈ 6..h-2, ofw ∈ 5..slot_w-1) at random position within the group's slot, in OUTER COLOR drawn from {2..9}; (b) OPTIONALLY a NESTED INNER FRAME 2 cells inside the outer, in a distinct INNER COLOR (when nested=True and dims allow); (c) ONE COLOR-1 MARKER DOT placed strictly INSIDE the innermost frame's interior. Rule (FOR EACH COLOR-1 MARKER, RECOLOR IT TO THE COLOR OF THE SMALLEST FRAME THAT STRICTLY ENCLOSES IT): FIND all color-1 marker cells and all rectangular FRAME outlines (each in its own color). For EACH marker at (mr, mc): FIND all frames whose interior contains the marker. SELECT the frame with the SMALLEST AREA (or smallest enclosing area). RECOLOR the marker cell to that frame's color. The original color-1 is replaced. Net: nested-frame structure colors each interior dot by its tightest containment; markers gain frame-specific identity.
2 hollow rectangular frames in distinct colors with overlapping interior bboxes.

0-bg grid (h~9-12, w~9-12) with TWO NESTED COLOR-1 RECTANGULAR FRAMES: (a) OUTER FRAME — rectangular outline from (1, 1) to (h-2, w-2) painted in color 1 (border-only rectangle, interior cells stay 0); (b) INNER FRAME — rectangular outline from (3, 3) to (max(3, h-6), max(3, w-6)) also painted in color 1, nested strictly inside the outer frame. The two frames define DEPTHS: cells outside any frame have depth 0; cells inside the outer but outside the inner have depth 1; cells inside the inner frame have depth 2. Frame outlines themselves are color 1 (initially). All other cells are 0. Rule (PAINT EACH CELL'S DEPTH+1 ACCORDING TO FRAME NESTING): keep color-1 frame cells AS 1. For EACH 0-cell, COMPUTE its DEPTH = number of color-1 rectangular frames that strictly contain it. PAINT the cell with COLOR (depth + 1) using a fixed depth→color mapping per demos (e.g., depth 0 → color 1, depth 1 → color 2, depth 2 → color 3, etc.). Net: the nested rectangle structure becomes a layered cake of concentric colored bands inside the original color-1 frames.

0-bg grid (h, w ∈ 10-14) with: N_FRAMES ∈ 1-3 HOLLOW COLOR-7 (ORANGE) RECTANGULAR FRAMES, each rh × rw (rh, rw ∈ 4-6) drawn via draw_rect_outline at non-overlapping interior positions (1-cell padding between frames via bbox-distance check). Each frame's INTERIOR (cells strictly inside the outline) starts EMPTY (color 0). Rule (FOR EACH HOLLOW ORANGE FRAME, FILL ITS INTERIOR WITH COLOR 8 (CYAN); FRAME OUTLINE STAYS ORANGE): IDENTIFY every 4-connected COLOR-7 component. For EACH frame: COMPUTE its bbox (rmin, cmin, rmax, cmax). For EVERY (r, c) with rmin < r < rmax AND cmin < c < cmax (strictly interior): IF g[r][c] == 0: PAINT g[r][c] = COLOR 8 (cyan). The frame outline (7s) stays 7. Cells outside any frame stay 0. Net: each orange frame's hollow center fills with cyan, turning frames into orange-bordered cyan blocks.

0-bg grid (size varies) with K (3-4) nested concentric color-4 frames and a control cell (1 or 2). Rule: outer = frames[control-1], inner = frames[control]; fill the ring between them (strictly inside outer, not inside inner) with 8. The grid size, frames and control value vary freely (was a fixed setup, ~26 distinct).
5-frames; rule fills square holes with 2.

0-bg grid (h 10..20, w 12..22) with 2-4 hollow gray(5) rectangle frames (distinct interior areas) and 2-4 arbitrary-shaped movers (distinct non-5 colors, distinct cell counts 1..5; singletons, dominoes, bars, L/S/T tetrominoes, plus/T/V/W pentominoes). Rule: rank frames by interior area and movers by size, then stamp each mover's normalized shape centered into the same-rank frame's interior on a blank canvas.

A 0-background grid contains 2-4 same-size rectangular frames and 1-3 differently sized distractor frames, all in distinct colors and separated by background. Exactly one same-size frame is the template: its interior contains a non-empty, non-solid pattern in its own color. The oracle keeps all frames matching the template's interior height and width, copies the relative pattern into each in that frame's color, and erases every mismatched frame.

0-bg grid (size varies). Two input styles, both ranked-recolored by bbox area: (a) NESTED CONCENTRIC RINGS -- a mono-color set of nested rectangular frames each separated by a 1-cell gap (the canonical look); (b) SCATTERED BLOBS -- K (2-8) connected blobs of distinct bbox areas. Rule: rank the 4-connected objects by bbox area DESC and recolor on a blank grid -- largest 2, next 3, next 4, ... For rings this yields concentric color bands; for blobs, size-ranked recolor.

0-bg grid (h, w ~ 11-22) with difficulty-dependent COLOR-5 RECTANGULAR FRAMES (1-2 easy / 2-3 medium / 3-5 hard) of size fh × fw (4..5 each), each a complete border outline painted in COLOR 5. Frames are placed at non-overlapping non-touching positions (1-cell padding via _frame_free). Inside EACH FRAME's STRICT INTERIOR: ONE NON-{0, 5} DOT cell placed at a random interior position (dot_r, dot_c) ∈ (r1+1..r2-1, c1+1..c2-1), painted in a DISTINCT non-{0, 5} color drawn from {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9}. Each frame holds EXACTLY ONE inner dot. Rule (FOR EACH 5-RECT-OUTLINE FRAME, FILL ITS INTERIOR WITH THE INNER DOT'S COLOR): for EACH COLOR-5 RECTANGULAR FRAME: identify its bbox interior (rows r1+1..r2-1, cols c1+1..c2-1). find the EXACTLY ONE non-{0, 5} cell inside the interior — call its color D. PAINT every bg-0 cell in the interior with COLOR D. The dot stays color D (it's already D). The 5-frame border stays color 5. Net: each framed chamber fills entirely with its inner dot's color, and the dot is absorbed into the fill.

exploration_yield.falsifier: A stratified decoded evaluation with at least 100,000 exact target tokens in each supported length bucket, matched on task family/complexity and exposure, that shows materially worse exact match or normalized edit distance for long programs despite comparable teacher-forced token loss would falsify the no-reweight recommendation.
limitations: The bundled telemetry stores only per-task mean token loss, not exact numerator/denominator.

exploration_yield.smallest_next_action: Apply the dry-run-clean telemetry patch, collect exact loss sums/token counts, and run stratified decoded evaluation with exact match and normalized edit distance.
exploration_yield.stop_condition: Not met exactly: the bundled 82 windows omit exact per-task target-token denominators and decoded completion, so >=100k exact tokens per length bucket cannot be certified from current telemetry.
exploration_yield.summary: GROUP-token normalization is exactly token-equitable and invariant to micro-batch partition: the trainer backpropagates unnormalized token-loss sums and divides the accumulated gradient by the exact group target-token count. Long programs therefore receive more aggregate mass only in proportion to their number of equally weighted target tokens, not less per token. A float64 autograd probe matched the full token-mean gradient across four different partitions to at most 1.12e-16, while an equal-sequence objective was materially different. Combined with the prior 582-task controlled regression (standardized log-length coefficient -0.0308, t=-1.88), there is no evidence warranting a length reweighting. Exact decoded completion equity remains unresolved because all 82 bundled telemetry windows omit exact task token counts, loss numerators, exact match, and edit distance.

rivals.name: global_total_area_color
rivals.racket_source:
(rule!
 (lambda (grid)
   (let* ((regions (find-0-regions grid))
          (total
           (reduce
            (lambda (count region)
              (let ((cell (first region)))
                (if (enclosed? grid (first cell) (second cell))
                    (+ count (length region))
                    count)))
            0
            regions))
          (fill-color
           (cond
            ((<= total 8) 8)
            ((<= total 24) 4)
            (else 3))))
     (reduce
      (lambda (out region)
        (let ((cell (first region)))
          (if (enclosed? grid (first cell) (second cell))
              (recolor-cells out region fill-color)
              out)))
      grid
      regions))))
